memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall
celebrate it as a festival to the LORD-a lasting ordinance." - Ex 12:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God builds remembering into the life of His people. Not as an optional extra,
but as a lasting ordinance.

Why? Because we forget. We are people who forget quickly. Israel would be
grumbling about food within weeks of walking through the Red Sea. God knows
this about us, and rather than scolding us for it, He gives us practices that
keep the memory alive.

That is grace. God provides not only the deliverance but also the means of
remembering it.

On the night before He died, Jesus was keeping this very meal with His disciples
when He took bread and said, "Do this in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). He was
not abolishing Passover; He was revealing what it had always pointed to. The
Lord's Supper is the new memorial for the greater deliverance.

There is something important here for ordinary Christian life too. Regular
habits of remembering are not legalism. Reading Scripture, gathering with God's
people, breaking bread, keeping a record of answered prayer. These are not ways
to earn God's favour. They are how forgetful people hold on to what God has
already done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done for you that you have started to forget?
2. What regular practice helps you remember His faithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I forget so easily. Thank You for giving me ways to remember. Keep the
cross fresh in my heart. Amen.
